reason: the design fails 1 of its checks

findings.text:
DSFRSH-2: 1 part to fix
DSFRSH-2[no-code]: A new run of the same issue never skips a stage due to prior run output; the dispatch-unit skip guard is conditional on resume_mode so it does not activate for fresh runs covers: RQGUAR-2
  Given: An issue has prior completed runs with artifacts present in the git state branch; a new run is started with no --resume flag and no status=interrupted state file
  When: The dispatch loop runs
  Then: The count of stage.start events in the event log equals the total number of stages declared in the pipeline fixture (every stage dispatched, not just the first) [FIX IN DESIGN: The Then asserts "count of stage.start events equals the total number of stages declared in the pipeline fixture." The fixture used by this test (artifact-snapshot-coverage.yaml) declares two stages: `intake` (leaf) and `cyc` (type: cycle). In a fresh run, `cyc` emits `cycle.start`, not `stage.start`; its member `cycled` also does not emit `stage.start` in a fresh run — cycle-orchestrator.sh lines 1524–1526 state explicitly "Fresh runs and later resumed iterations receive no stage.start for cycle members via this path", and the test at lines 882–898 asserts `stage.start` count for `cycled` must equal 0 on a fresh run. Therefore the stage.start count for a fresh run with this fixture is 1 (intake only), not 2 (the declared stage count). The Then assertion "count == total declared stages" evaluates to "1 == 2" and would fail for correct behaviour. DSCYCL-1 (required cycle stage in the fixture) and the established cycle event semantics together make the Then unsatisfiable as written. — it cannot be true together with that; make them agree]
  And: No stage.skip event is emitted for any stage

answers: test-author finding 1: done — DSFRSH-2's Then clause was too vague ("Every stage emits a stage.start event") and led the test-author to write a narrow assertion checking only that intake emits one stage.start, which passes even if other stages never emit it. Changed the Then to "The count of stage.start events in the event log equals the total number of stages declared in the pipeline fixture (every stage dispatched, not just the first)". This requires the test to count all stage.start events across the fixture and assert the total equals the stage count — which fails if any stage is silently skipped. Added Finding 29 documenting the change.
